source.title: TASTE: Throughput-Aware Batch Size Tuning for On-Device Edge Learning
source.authors: Avik Bhatnagar; Federico Nicolás Peccia; Oliver Bringmann

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Compares batch-size conditions and held-out accuracy using an edge-training setup, including recipe adaptations; it does not measure train–test error gaps directly.
record.gate_note: Tests batch-size effects on test accuracy in supervised and online continual image classification. Throughput measurements are not rows because they do not measure the claim's generalization outcome. Training-error results are not reported.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out image-classification accuracy across batch sizes at fixed data-pass budgets: 200 supervised epochs and one online continual-learning pass. These results test V5 in an edge-learning setting, with gradient accumulation or learning-rate scaling.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: throughput-selected batches, combined with supervised gradient accumulation or continual-learning learning-rate scaling, yield accuracy comparable to reference configurations while improving edge-CPU throughput. This is their overall conclusion; individual supervised comparisons show dataset-dependent accuracy differences.
record.recipe_differences: Tests batch-size effects on ResNet-18 image classification with SGD, gradient accumulation, and learning-rate scaling. Evaluates on edge CPUs, including offline supervised training for 200 epochs and online continual learning for one pass.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies by dataset and training paradigm: smaller batches outperform larger ones on CIFAR-100 supervised learning, larger batches improve TinyImageNet supervised accuracy, and large batches degrade continual-learning accuracy relative to the reference.
record.peer_reviewed: Euromicro Symposium on Digital Systems Design
record.problems: The study reports test accuracy rather than training error or the train–test gap. Supervised-learning accuracy comparisons are described as comparable overall but show dataset-specific differences; the text does not provide exact supervised results for every batch size. CL comparisons use reference batch size 20 and maximum batch sizes, not a fixed epoch budget.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible batch-size/test-accuracy results are stated in text with recoverable values. Figures 4 and 6 show further accuracy curves, but precise figure-only values were not extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer-tuning scope.

Language models; longer-training remedies; warmup; controlled normalization or regularization changes; and whether recipe adaptations remove a previously measured penalty. No unadapted-versus-adapted ablation is reported.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. Held-out accuracy at a fixed epoch or pass budget suffices to test V5; training error and a directly measured train–test gap are not required. Micro-batch size and effective optimizer batch size must be distinguished. Comparable accuracy at batches 4–20 does not establish that these sizes exceed a workload-dependent threshold, and does not independently demonstrate recovery from a large-batch penalty. Additional figure curves and other-dataset degradation are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.

Language models; a workload-dependent batch-size threshold; and direct train–test error gaps. The supervised comparison uses a fixed 200 epochs; online continual learning uses a single pass. The study also tests learning-rate scaling and gradient accumulation.
Sharpness and other measured properties as predictors of the generalization gap.

source_check.notes: Supervised learning uses learning rate 0.1 for 200 epochs; continual learning uses one pass, scaled learning rates, and experience replay.
